<reason>Both sides were sharp and stayed on the motion, but PRO's structural dilemma survived the exchange better than CON's textual gotcha. CON's strongest mechanism — a crewed submersible covers "a postage stamp of bottom," so blank squares are a sonar/AUV problem — was largely defused when PRO reframed parity as an ocean programme structured like a space programme, where crew hours are a minority slice and the bulk of the money buys exactly the autonomous fleets CON calls cheap; that directly answers "divergence at the first hull." CON's pretext attack (PRO's "yes, I'd still want parity if the floor were mapped") landed a real hit, but PRO answered it honestly and turned it: Mars is already mapped to metre scale and CON still defends the crewed premium there, so mapping status cannot be the governing criterion on CON's own account either. That forced CON onto a substitution test, which PRO showed cuts space first (rovers, orbiters, sample return), while CON's fallback to "presence and political-scientific capability" quietly concedes the constituency value it mocks when PRO invokes it for the ocean. CON handled the capacity question honestly and turned it plausibly ("the niche is small"), and its opportunity-cost/centre-of-gravity point was the best remaining CON material, but it stayed more asserted than demonstrated. CON also never cleanly exposed the weakest seam in PRO's disjunction — that parity-by-subtraction satisfies the motion vacuously — settling for "that is a different fight." PRO's clipped opening is an execution cost, and its late "vote for value returned" drifts slightly from the given clause, which keeps the margin narrow rather than comfortable.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's reply to the pretext trap: conceding "yes" and immediately turning it — Mars is mapped to metre scale yet CON still defends crewed spaceflight there, so "unmapped" was never anyone's terminus; blank squares are the symptom of the funding gap, not the whole warrant. That neutralized CON's cleanest motion-anchored kill shot and pushed CON onto a substitution criterion that PRO showed deletes astronauts before submersibles.</best_rebuttal>
